title: The Spanish Empire and Its Legacy: Fiscal Redistribution
author: Regina Grafe y Alejandra Irigoin
desc: El sistema fiscal español no fue ni la máquina extractiva de los dependentistas ni una etapa de Estado moderno. Fue un complejo sistema de redistribución fiscal dentro de América.
tesis: Grafe e Irigoin desafían tanto a los dependentistas (que ven la colonia como pura extracción) como a los modernizadores (que ven la España imperial como Estado moderno). El sistema fiscal español fue más complejo: una parte significativa de la recaudación se quedaba y redistribuía dentro de América. La realidad colonial no fue ni el saqueo total ni el desarrollo autónomo — fue un sistema de negociación fiscal entre virreyes, cabildos y la Corona.
ideas: El sistema fiscal colonial no fue pura extracción: parte significativa de la recaudación se redistribuía dentro de América.
Las élites coloniales negociaban permanentemente con la Corona — el imperio no era monolítico.
La tesis dependentista del saqueo total necesita matizarse sin por ello negar la explotación colonial.
contexto: Artículo académico publicado en 2006 por Regina Grafe (Northwestern University) y Alejandra Irigoin (London School of Economics). Forma parte del debate historiográfico sobre el carácter del imperio español que se intensificó a principios del siglo XXI, cuando nuevos datos fiscales coloniales permitieron cuestionar tanto la tesis dependentista del saqueo total como la visión modernizadora del Estado colonial.

conexiones.razon: Semo analiza el capitalismo colonial que el sistema fiscal de Grafe redistribuía parcialmente.
La complejidad fiscal que Grafe documenta matiza el modelo de sistema-mundo de Wallerstein.

tl: Mexico y Veracruz: primeras cajas reales del Imperio
Of the 72 local treasuries studied over a period of more than 250 years, 14 cajas were created before 1600, corresponding to Mexico and Veracruz (1520s), Cuzco and Lima (1530s).
Lima y Cuzco: la red fiscal llega al Pacifico andino
In Peru, e.g. Lima acted as the caja general, Trujillo, Huamanga, Cuzco and Arequipa functioned as cajas principales and Arica and Pasco as subordinate cajas.
Potosi y Zacatecas: las cajas de la plata
Santiago de Chile, Merida and Guadalajara in the 1540s, Potosi, Zacatecas and Huancavelica in the 1550-70s, Durango, Acapulco, Arequipa and Arica by the 1590s.
Lima reenvia 64% de su recaudacion a Espana
In the 1590s about 64 percent of the revenue collected by Lima was transhipped to Spain but after the 1660s even here they never exceeded ten percent. The picture for Mexico was comparable.
Felipe III crea los Tribunales de Cuentas en Lima, Bogota y Mexico
In 1605 Philip III created the first Tribunales de Cuentas in Lima, Bogota and Mexico, a supervisory and auditing agency, which oversaw the work of the royal treasury officials.
Mexico remite la mitad de sus rentas a Castilla y Manila
In Mexico between 1590 and 1640 roughly half of all crown revenue was remitted either to Castile or the Philippines, though we do not know how much of this went to either place.
Las remesas limenas a Espana se desploman a 1%

It plummeted between 1660 from 12 percent to 1 percent in the 1680s and did not rise over 10 percent. At the same time more money went to the garrisons Concepción, Chiloe and Valdivia, Panama, Callao and Guayaquil.
Carlos III crea 27 nuevas cajas tras la guerra de los Siete Anos

Between 1700 and 1760 ten new cajas were established, and from the reign of Charles III in the 1760s 27 more treasury districts appeared. Eighteen of these were established in the newly created Viceroyalty of the River Plate.
La alcabala se extiende a alimentos basicos y reventan revueltas

In 1776 the alcabala was extended to staple foodstuffs (chuño, charqui, ají, aguardiente), as well as to tobacco, sugar and native textiles in Peru. The Crown then tried to charge the tax on grain and maize.
En Nueva Espana las alcabalas rinden mas que la plata

In late colonial times alcabalas yielded 14 percent of total revenues in Peru, 24 in percent Chile and six percent in the Upper Peru. Already in 1780 alcabalas rendered more than silver taxes to the Mexican Treasury.
El 45% de la recaudacion colonial circula entre cajas
Up to 45 percent of the revenue raised in colonial Spanish cajas in the late 18th century was not spent in the same district. Thus, our tables illustrate three basic features of Spanish imperialism.
Cuba recibe 68 millones de pesos en situados
The best number for the monies actually received in Cuba as situados is de la Sagra's account of 68,641,605 pesos between 1788 and 1804 of about 4 Mio per year.
Manila vive del situado mexicano del Galeon
Manila received 1,144,138 pesos between 1791 and 95 and 4,341,623 pesos between 1796-1800. During the following two five year periods these fell to 1.8-1.9 Mio pesos.
Cartagena recibe 17 millones de pesos del interior

The latter received about 17 million pesos from the interior regions in New Granada over the period 1776-1810, roughly 25 pesos per capita for the whole district population, or 119 pesos extra for every inhabitant of the port.
Buenos Aires recibe 19.85 pesos per capita en transferencias

Transfers of 20 pesos or more per annum to places like Havana, Buenos Aires and Cartagena enriched and empowered elites in both sending and receiving region because the management of transfers remained in the hands of mercantile interests.
Napoleón captura a los Borbones y quiebra la soberanía
In May 1808 Charles IV was imprisoned by French troops. Napoleon placed his brother Joseph on the throne of Spain and demanded that the regular transfers of silver be continued as before.
Los aduanas de Buenos Aires y La Habana se multiplican por diez

Meanwhile in Buenos Aires and Havana yields from customs increased 10 times from 1778 to 1803-05. This is the lowest bound estimate at least for the increase in trade since contraband was the norm in the River Plate.
El imperio se fragmenta en estados fiscalmente autonomos

Regional elites seized colonial revenues immediately to defend their political and economic interests and in time to define the fiscal boundaries of new republican states. Fiscal revenues and mint houses fell into the hands of new local authorities.
